info.title: Message Vault HTTP API
info.description: HTTP API for a local Message Vault. Bearer session tokens come from login. API tokens come from Settings → Account.

get.summary: Report process liveness.

List the accounts this vault holds, with their flags, message count, and
storage use. The owner's own account is not among them: the list holds
the users of this vault, and the owner is not one of them.

post.summary: Create an account.
post.description:
The vault owner may always: the owner picks the first password and the
account holder replaces it at first sign-in, so the owner's choice survives
one session and no longer. A stranger with no credential may while the
vault is open, and is signed in on creation. Registering is the vault's
only self-service door, shut unless the owner has opened it; an unclaimed
vault is shut too, because its first act is being claimed, not being
joined.

403.description: The vault is closed, or the credential is not the owner's

get.summary: Read one account: the owner reads any, an account reads its own.

delete.summary:
Permanently delete an account: login, profile, contacts, and every
message it owns, with its data directory.
delete.description:
The vault owner deletes any account outright, the demo account included,
which is how a demo vault is cleared into a real one. An account deletes
itself with a body carrying the confirmation and its current password: a
credential belongs in a body, not in a URL or a header of the vault's own
invention, and a DELETE body has no defined meaning in RFC 9110 but is not
forbidden. The demo account refuses its own deletion, and nobody deletes
the owner.

requestBody.description: Sent by an account deleting itself; the owner sends no body

patch.summary:
Change an account. The account itself sets its display name, time zone
and handles; the vault owner sets another account's disabled flag and
its import, export and delete permissions. A field the caller may not
set answers `403 Forbidden`, and the reloaded account is the answer.

get.summary: List the account's named API tokens with their permissions and masked secrets.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Account id; must be the caller's own

post.summary:
Create a named API token. Returns the plaintext secret once, at creation;
it is never returned again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Account id; must be the caller's own

delete.summary: Delete one named API token. Requests using it start failing on the next call.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Account id; must be the caller's own

patch.summary: Rename one named API token. The label is trimmed before storing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Account id; must be the caller's own

delete.summary:
Destroy one account's conversations, messages, and attachments. The
account itself, its contacts, and its login survive.
delete.description:
The vault owner may, on any account. The account itself may with a
credential that carries the `delete` scope, session or API token, and
confirms in the body.

requestBody.description: Sent by an account deleting its own messages; the owner sends no body

put.description:
An account changing its own must supply the current one; the change
revokes its API tokens and answers `200` with a rotated session token.
The vault owner sets another account's without the current one and
answers `204`: that account's sessions end, and its holder signs in with
the new password and is made to replace it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Account id whose password is set

200.description: Own password changed; the rotated session token

204.description: Password set by the vault owner; the account's sessions are ended

get.summary:
Attachment storage usage for an account: total bytes, count, and the 100
largest files. The owner reads any account's; an account reads its own.
Download a previously stored content-addressed asset (read-only).
get.description: The body streams the stored bytes; the URL is the SHA-256 fingerprint.

put.summary: Store one asset body under its SHA-256 fingerprint.

head.summary: Probe whether a content-addressed asset is already stored (no body).
head.description: Clients may skip sending bytes when the asset exists.

post.summary: Start a chunked (multipart) asset upload and get the part size.

200.description: The asset is already stored; nothing was created

delete.summary: Abort and delete a chunked asset upload's staging files.

post.summary:
Assemble the uploaded parts, verify the SHA-256 fingerprint, and install
the asset.

put.summary: Write one part of a chunked asset upload.

get.summary: The account's Contact Groups, A–Z.

post.summary: Create a Contact Group.

delete.summary: Delete a Contact Group and its memberships.

get.summary: Contact ids in one Contact Group.

patch.summary: Put contacts in and take contacts out of one Contact Group.

get.summary: Page through the account's contacts (id, name, handles, groups).

post.summary:
Load a VCF or vCard CSV address book into this account. The body is the
file itself, and `Content-Type` says which: `text/vcard` or `text/csv`.
post.description:
This is a standalone act against the vault, never part of an Import Run:
contacts are vault state, and a person may load them before or after
bringing messages in. Only the rows the address book owns are replaced, so
Contact Groups, names the person typed, and identities an import discovered
all survive. How the file is read is the open question in #270; this route
is where that answer lands.

requestBody.description: The address book file: a vCard file as text/vcard, or a vCard CSV export as text/csv.

post.summary: First/last message dates and counts for a list of contact ids.
Report which identifiers this account has no vault contact for.

get.summary:
Full contact view: per-handle services, message stats, and group
memberships.

delete.summary:
Delete a trashed contact the way a phone's Delete Contact does: the name
and the person's edits go, the contact becomes Unknown again and leaves
the trash, and every conversation it was in stays as it is, showing the
handle. Conversations are never deleted with a contact. A contact that is
not in the trash answers 409.

204.description: Deleted: the contact is Unknown again

409.description: The contact is not in the trash

patch.summary: Rename a contact or change its linked handles.

post.summary:
Take a contact out of the trash. Idempotent: restoring a contact that
was not trashed still answers 204.

Put a contact in the trash. Idempotent: trashing an already-trashed
contact still answers 204.

get.summary:
Page through conversations with participants, message counts, and tags.
Newest activity first unless `sort` says otherwise.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Conversation search; empty lists all non-trashed

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated keys, `-` for descending: `date` (last message) or `messages` (message count). Default `-date`.

get.summary:
One conversation, in the same shape a list row already has — so a caller
that opens a thread from a list does not have to convert between two
shapes, and paging through the whole list to find one id is never
necessary. Trash is a property the list applies, not a gate on reading:
a trashed conversation still answers here.

delete.summary:
Permanently delete a trashed conversation: the conversation, its
messages, and any attachment file no other message still uses. Trash is
the only door to deletion, so a conversation that is not in the trash
answers 409 rather than being deleted from wherever it was.

409.description: The conversation is not in the trash

get.summary:
A conversation's messages, ascending by timestamp then `sort_order`. The
read path a screen uses to open a thread: no search query to compose,
just the conversation id.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Narrow to one calendar year, in the vault's stored offset

post.summary:
Take a conversation out of the trash. Idempotent: restoring a
conversation that was not trashed still answers 204.

get.summary: Per-backup message counts for one conversation (the Sources panel).

post.summary:
Put a conversation in the trash. Idempotent: trashing an
already-trashed conversation still answers 204.

get.summary:
The account's Export Runs as a page, newest first unless `sort` says
otherwise, narrowed to one `status` when given.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: One of running, completed, failed, cancelled

post.summary:
Start an Export Run: compile the scope, count what it matches, and
record the run as `running`. Read its messages at
`GET /v1/exports/{id}/messages`, then close it with `complete` or `cancel`.

get.summary: One Export Run.

post.summary: Record that the client gave the run up.
Record that the client finished reading the run.

get.summary:
The messages a running Export Run's scope selects, a page at a time,
oldest first unless `sort` says otherwise. Each page read raises the
run's `messages_delivered` to the rows handed over so far.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Page offset; no cap, an offset past the end is an empty page

409.description: The run is no longer running

get.summary:
The account's Import Runs, newest first, as a page. `status=running`
finds the one run the desktop app may resume.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: One of running, completed, completed_with_issues, failed, cancelled

post.summary:
Start an import session and return its id. Finish the session at
POST /v1/imports/{id}/complete.

409.description: The account already has an active import session

get.summary: Status, timings, and issues for one import session.

post.summary: Import one message-ir JSONL body into the vault.

requestBody.description: message-ir JSONL as application/x-ndjson or application/jsonl. Attachments are uploaded first by SHA-256 through /v1/assets.

415.description: The body is not JSON Lines (multipart/form-data is not accepted)

post.summary: Record the outcome of an import session started with POST /v1/imports.

get.summary: List the contacts one import run created or changed, newest first.
get.description:
New and changed are told apart by comparing each contact's `created_at`
against the moment the run started: a contact first recorded during the run
is new, one merely touched is changed. How many of each the run made is on
the run's own record, `GET /v1/imports/{id}`.

post.summary: Discard a live import session, freeing the account's single slot.
Move a live import session to another stage.

get.summary: The account's Message Tags, A–Z.

post.summary: Create a Message Tag.

delete.summary: Delete a Message Tag and its memberships.

get.summary: Conversation ids in one Message Tag.

patch.summary: Put conversations in and take conversations out of one Message Tag.

get.summary:
Messages matching `q`, oldest first unless `sort` says otherwise: the same
rows an Export Run with a `query` scope would hand over, behind a signed-in
session with the list defaults and the list's offset ceiling.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search query in the Messages list's words; empty matches every message

get.summary:
One message by id: the row the Messages list would show, looked up
directly.
get.description:
Read-only. A message is never written through this route: an import
writes messages, and trashing is a conversation operation
(`docs/agents/http-api-rules.md`, "Methods"). The lookup carries the
list's own defaults — the caller's account, no trashed conversation, no
duplicate — so a row the list hides is `404` here too, and a link out of
a search result never reaches further than the search did.

get.summary: List the account's saved searches, A–Z.

post.summary:
Create a saved search: `201 Created`, `Location: /v1/saved-searches/{id}`,
and the row.

Location.description: Path of the new saved search

delete.description:
Deleting an import-created saved search removes the shortcut only. The
`vault_imports` row it pointed at is the account's permanent record of that
run and is never touched here.

patch.summary: Replace a saved search's name and query, and return it.

get.summary: The search words one list accepts.

The Session the bearer token names: its account, username, and import
sources. A session token and an API token both answer, because a program
checking its token needs the same facts as a browser restoring a sign-in.

post.summary:
Sign in: verify a local username and password and answer the Session, a
`201 Created` whose `Location` is the singleton itself.

delete.summary: Sign out: revoke the presented session token, ending the Session.

Empty the trash: every trashed conversation is deleted for good, with
its messages and any attachment file no other message uses, and every
trashed contact loses its name and details and becomes Unknown, its
conversations untouched. Trash is the only door to permanent deletion;
this is the door for everything in it at once.

get.summary: Report whether this vault is unclaimed, closed, or open.

post.summary: Claim an unclaimed vault by creating its owner.
post.description:
Unauthenticated, because a vault with no owner has no credential that
could authorize this. Whoever reaches an unclaimed vault first may claim
it: the vault is self-hosted, so its operator installs the software,
claims the vault, and publishes the port, in that order and at times of
their choosing. An unclaimed vault is also empty, so a lost race destroys
nothing and announces itself at once.

get.summary: Read the vault's settings.

AccountResponse.description:
One account: who it is, what it may do, and how much it holds. The owner
and the account itself both read the whole struct; nothing in it is a
message.

emails.description: Email addresses linked to the account.

is_demo.description: True for the seeded demo account (cannot be deleted).

is_owner.description: True for the vault owner: manages accounts, holds no messages.

must_change_password.description:
The vault owner chose this password; it must be replaced before the
account can be used.

must_set_up_profile.description:
The account holder has not set up their profile yet, so profile setup
is owed before the account can be used. The vault decides this, not the
client: the same answer reaches every app, and it survives cleared site
data and a second browser.

phones.description: Phone handles linked to the account.

time_zone.description:
IANA time zone every message time, day and year is shown in, for
example `America/New_York`. Chosen at profile setup.

AccountStorageResponse.description: Attachment usage and the largest files.

AddressBookLoadResponse.description: What loading an address book changed.

phones.description: Phone identities linked to those contacts.

phones_needing_review.description: Identities written with a review note (an ambiguous number).

ApiTokenItem.description: One named API token as shown in Settings: label, permissions, and masked secret.

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix-seconds string.

disabled.description: True when the token is disabled and rejects requests.

expires_at.description: Unix-seconds expiry; absent means no expiry.

id.description: Token id (the secret itself is stored hashed).

last_accessed_at.description: Unix-seconds string of last use; absent when never used.

AssetUploadStartBody.description: Total bytes and optional MIME type for a chunked upload.

AssetUploadStartResponse.description: Upload id and part size, or the already-stored asset.

Attachment.description: One attachment of an exported message.

missing_reason.description: Why the file is missing, when it is.

sha256.description: Content fingerprint of the stored bytes.

password.description: Password for the vault owner. Must satisfy the vault's password policy.

username.description: Login username for the vault owner.

CompleteImportBody.description: Final stats and issues for a finished import session.

status.description:
Explicit session outcome; overrides `ok` when present.
One of `completed`, `completed_with_issues`, `failed`.

CompleteImportIssueBody.description: One parse/convert/upload issue from the import.

ContactDetail.description: Full contact view: every handle with stats, plus totals across them.

group_conversations.description: Group conversations the contact appears in.

handles.description: Every handle linked to the contact, with per-handle stats.

last_modified.description: When the contact’s address-book shape last changed (`datetime('now')`).

total_messages.description: Messages across all of the contact's conversations.

ContactHandleInfo.description: One handle on a contact with service and message stats.

end_date.description: Date of the last message involving this handle.

group_conversations.description: Group conversations this handle appears in.

group_message_count.description: Messages in group conversations involving this handle.

individual_message_count.description: Messages in 1:1 conversations involving this handle.

service.description: Platform service, e.g. `whatsapp`, when the handle is linked with one.

start_date.description: Date of the first message involving this handle.

ContactHandlePayload.description: A handle value plus optional platform service.

service.description: Platform service (`phone`, `email`, or `whatsapp`); inferred when omitted.

ContactMutationBody.description: Body for `PATCH /v1/contacts/{id}`. Exactly one mutation field should be set.

name.description: New display name; `None` leaves it unchanged.

service.description: Platform service, when the handle is linked with one.

ContactSelectionSummary.description: Contact-level first/last seen and message counts for the selection table.

end_date.description: Date of the contact's last message.

group_message_count.description: Messages in group conversations with the contact.

individual_message_count.description: Messages in 1:1 conversations with the contact.

start_date.description: Date of the contact's first message.

ids.description: Contact ids to summarize; an empty list covers every contact.

ContactSummary.description: Contact row for the list: name, handles, groups.

handle_count.description: Number of handles linked to the contact.

handles.description: Normalized (and raw when distinct) handle values for client-side filter.

last_modified.description: When the contact’s address-book shape last changed (`datetime('now')`).

ContactUpdateHandlePayload.description: The previous and new handle values for a link change.

service.description: Platform service for the new handle.

ConversationSourceInfo.description: One backup source with message counts and share.

message_count.description: Messages in this conversation from this source.

percentage.description: Share of the conversation's unique messages, 0–100.

unique_count.description: Messages only this source has (not hidden duplicates).

ConversationSummary.description: Conversation row for the list: participants, counts, tags.

date_range_end.description: Timestamp of the conversation's last message.

date_range_start.description: Timestamp of the conversation's first message.

id.description: The conversation's id; search for it as `in:#<id>`.

label.description: Group label from the export, when present.

message_count.description: Messages in the conversation (excluding hidden duplicates).

service.description: Platform service of the conversation, e.g. `imessage`.

CreateAccountRequest.description: Body for creating an account, by the vault owner or by a stranger.

password.description:
Local password. The owner must give one, and the account holder
replaces it at first sign-in. A stranger may leave it absent or empty
to open an account with no password.

phone.description: Phone number linked to the account.

preferred_name.description: Display name shown in the vault.

CreateApiTokenRequest.description: Body for creating a token: label, permissions, optional expiry.

can_delete.description: May destroy message data. Default false — asked for, never inherited.

can_export.description: May call the export endpoints. Default true.

can_import.description: May call the import endpoints. Default true.

expires_in_days.description: Days until expiry. Omit for the default (365 days). Pass `0` for no expiry.

CreateApiTokenResponse.description: The created token, including its plaintext secret (returned once).

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix-seconds string.

expires_at.description: Unix-seconds expiry; absent means no expiry.

token.description: Plaintext secret — returned once at creation.

token_hint.description: Masked form for the Settings list (also persisted).

CreateExportBody.description: Body of `POST /v1/exports`: the scope, and the tool that asked.

tool.description: Client/tool name recorded on the run, e.g. `vault-pull`.

CreateImportBody.description:
Source, mode, dedupe and tool for a new Import Run. The bearer token
names the account.

dedupe.description: Run cross-source soft-dedupe after each batch.

device_id.description: Which install is creating the session.

form.description:
Import form snapshot, stored so the screen can be restored.

Credentials are stripped before storage: a `backupPassword` or
`whatsappKey` posted here is dropped rather than persisted.

source_fingerprint.description: Source path, size, mtime, and message count.

source_identities.description: Addresses the backup's device sent from, when the client read them.

stage.description: Stage the run opens at. Defaults to `parse`.

staging_dir.description: Absolute staging path on the client that owns this session.

CreateSessionRequest.description: Username and password, the body of `POST /v1/session`.

token.description:
Session token to send as `Authorization: Bearer …`. Present only when
a stranger registered, because they are signed in on creation.

CreatedAccountResponse.description:
The account that was created, and the Session a stranger's registration
opens on it. The owner's creation opens no session, so `token` is absent.

DeleteAccountRequest.description:
Confirmation flag and the current password when one is set: the body an
account sends to delete itself. The owner sends none.

confirm.description: Must be `true`; anything else is rejected.

current_password.description: Required when the account has a local password.

DeleteMessagesRequest.description:
Confirmation flag: the body an account sends to delete its own messages.
The owner sends none.

confirm.description: Must be `true`; anything else is rejected.

DeleteMessagesResponse.description: Counts of deleted conversations and attachment rows.

attachments.description: Attachment rows deleted (on-disk files are removed too).

DiscardImportResponse.description: Confirmation that a session was discarded.

ExportRun.description:
One Export Run: what was asked for and how much matched, never what
the messages said. `POST /v1/exports` creates one, every route under
`/v1/exports/{id}` answers it.

attachment_count.description: Distinct attachment fingerprints among the matching messages.

conversation_count.description: Distinct conversations with at least one matching message.

finished_at.description: UTC time the run finished, when it has.

message_count.description: Messages the scope matched when the run was created.

messages_delivered.description:
Rows handed over so far through `GET /v1/exports/{id}/messages`,
so an abandoned run shows how far it got.

scope.description: What the run asked for, as given.

tool.description: Exporting tool, e.g. `vault-pull`, when the client named one.

total_bytes.description: Sum of the known sizes of those distinct attachments, in bytes.

oneOf.description: Every non-trashed message the account holds.
The messages a query in the search language matches.

q.description:
The query, as typed. Never blank: an empty query is the
`everything` form.

oneOf.description:
Conversations and messages picked by hand. A message is selected when
its conversation is listed or it is listed itself; either list may be
empty, but not both.

conversation_ids.description: Conversation ids whose every message is exported.

message_ids.description: Message ids exported on their own.

ExportScope.description:
What an Export Run asked for, stored as given (`docs/agents/http-api-rules.md`,
"Runs"). One of three forms: everything the account holds, a query in the
search language, or conversations and messages picked by hand.

FieldDoc.description: One word as the web and the docs see it.

value_type.description: What shape of value it takes.

values.description: Keyword or fixed values the word accepts.

ImportContactRow.description: One contact an import run touched, and whether the run created it.

is_new.description:
True when this run created the contact, false when it only changed one
that already existed.

name.description: Preferred name; empty when the run learned an address and no name.

ImportMode.description:
What happens to a source's messages that were imported before: `replace`
wipes them first, `append` keeps them and adds only new ones.

ImportResponse.description: Import result: stats plus optional dedupe counts.

ImportStats.description: Counters for one import run (staging and promote results).

assets_copied.description: Unique media files written to the asset store.

assets_deduped.description: Media files already present under the same fingerprint, skipped.

assets_missing.description: Attachment files referenced but not found on disk.

contacts.description: Contacts loaded from the address book.

contacts_created.description: Contacts the import created for participants nothing else owned.

contacts_skipped.description: True when the address book was not loaded (already present or no file).

messages_appended.description: Messages added by an append-mode import.

messages_deduped.description: Messages hidden as duplicates within this import.

phones_needing_review.description: Flagged phone handles (ambiguous; review note set) inserted by this import.

ImportSummary.description:
One Import Run as `GET /v1/imports` lists it: the counts Settings shows,

dedupe.description: Whether cross-source dedupe runs after each batch.

stage.description: Where a running run is; null once it is over.

staging_dir.description: Absolute path to the staging folder on the client that owns the run.

summary.description:
What the user approved at the last gate they passed, or null. The

Which list a query is compiled for. Each list accepts its own subset of

Participant.description:
One participant of a conversation, carrying the name to show for them:
the Contact's name, else what that backup called them in that
conversation, else the handle.

contact_id.description:
Linked vault contact id: when the handle is on a Contact, or — for a
participant with no handle — the contact the vault bound the name to
directly, since that is the only place the link is recorded for
them. Matches the `id` every other contact shape uses, so a caller
can compare the two without converting either.

handle.description:
Raw handle value (phone, email, or username). `None` when the source
named this person without recording any address for them.

name.description:
What to show for this person. Never empty — the vault falls back to
the handle when nothing else names them, and to the name alone for
someone a backup named without recording any address.

service.description:
Platform service, e.g. `imessage`. `None` for the same reason as
`handle`: with no address there is nothing to carry a service on.

PatchAccountRequest.description:
Body for changing an account. Omitted fields are left alone. The name,
zone and handles are the account's own to set; the disabled flag and the
three permissions are the vault owner's.

can_delete.description: Allow or forbid deleting message data.

handles.description: Handles to add/link onto the account profile.

preferred_name.description: Display name to set; `None` (or empty) leaves the current name unchanged.

remove_handles.description: Handles to unlink from the account profile.

time_zone.description:
IANA time zone to set, for example `America/New_York`; `None` leaves
the current zone unchanged. An unknown name is a 422.

PatchVaultSettingsRequest.description: Body for changing the vault's settings. Omitted fields are left alone.

public_registration.description: Let anyone reaching the vault create their own account, or stop them.

Problem.description:
An RFC 7807 problem document: the body of every failure the vault answers,
served as `application/problem+json` (`docs/agents/http-api-rules.md`).

`type` is the URL of the page describing this kind of failure, one page per
type, or `about:blank` for an internal error. A validation failure carries
`errors`, every field that failed, in place of `detail`. Every problem
repeats the response's `x-request-id` as `request_id`, so the person
reading the failure and the operator reading the log are looking at the
same request.

The extension members belong to one type each: `word` and `did_you_mean`
to `search-query-invalid`, `retry_after` to `rate-limited`.

detail.description:
One sentence about this occurrence. Absent on a validation failure,
which lists `errors` instead.

did_you_mean.description:
`search-query-invalid`: a word the language does have, within a small
edit distance of the one used.

errors.description:
Every rule the request broke, one sentence each. Only on
`validation-failed`.

request_id.description: The `x-request-id` of the response this came in.

retry_after.description:
`rate-limited`: seconds until an attempt may succeed, the same figure
as the `Retry-After` header.

status.description: The HTTP status, repeated in the body.

type.description:
URL of the page describing this kind of failure; `about:blank` for a
`500 Internal Server Error`.

SetImportStageBody.description: New stage for a live session.

summary.description:
What the user approved at the gate they just passed, when they passed one.

Recorded here rather than at completion so an approval survives a
reload: the summary shown at a gate is recomputed from the folder, but
what was approved is a different question and only the session
remembers it. Absent leaves the stored `summary_json` untouched —
most stage changes carry nothing, and treating absent as null would
throw away the plan the outcome is later judged against.

token.description: Replacement session token (the previous one is revoked).
